title: Prehabilitation for Periacetabular Osteotomy Surgery.
official: Pilot Study of the Effect Physiotherapy Led Prehabilitation Has on Hip Function and Strength Following Peri-acetabular Osteotomy for the Management of Idiopathic Adolescent Hip Dysplasia.
summary:
This study is designed to investigate the impact of a patient specific physiotherapy prehabilitation programme on the outcomes of patients presenting with symptomatic hip dysplasia.

Prehabilitation for peri-acetabular osteotomy (PAO) surgery has not previously been investigated and we do not know the effect it would have on the post-surgical outcomes.

A clinical study is required to investigate the impact formal prehabilitation has on patients undergoing PAO. The investigators will carry out a pilot project to ensure the investigators have the right study design with appropriate outcomes, and that children and families will consent to taking part.

The pilot project will be funded by The Children's Hospital Charity (TCHC). Once successfully completed, the investigators will apply for funding for a large scale, multicentre trial.

Following completion of our research project the investigators will be able to advise patients on the expected effect of prehabilitation on the outcomes of this surgery.

The investigators hypothesise that patients who have a period of prehabilitation prior to surgery will have better physical outcome measures and hip outcome scores compared to those who do not have prehabilitation.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Idiopathic hip dysplasia listed for PAO surgery
* Able to attend physiotherapy assessment and follow-up at Sheffield Children's Hospital

Exclusion Criteria:

* Unable to follow instruction and carry out a home exercise programme safely and independently
* PAO surgery not an appropriate treatment option
* Tonnis 2 or greater radiographic changes
* Incongruent hip joint / salvage hip surgery
